newsitem.title: CANADA: Interest high in Wascana rival bid - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Interest high in Wascana rival bid - CEO.

text.p: Interest in the possibility of mounting a rival bid to Talisman Energy Inc's offer for Wascana Energy Inc is strong, Wascana's chief executive Frank Proto said on Friday.

"The interest is high and I think that's known around Calgary," Proto said in a telephone interview. "We've now had to open a second data room...and I've just come from a meeting where we've discussed whether or not it's going to be necessary to open a third."
Wascana said this week its board was reviewing Talisman's C$1.7 billion offer and had opened data rooms in Calgary.

Proto declined to give his opinion on how Talisman's offer -- C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share -- measured up to his own view of Wascana's value because the company's board had yet rule on the bid.
But he disputed a number of criticisms made earlier on Friday by Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee regarding Wascana's financial and operating projections.
In particular, he took aim at Buckee's statement that Wascana would have to have drilled a third of its budgeted wells by now to achieve its production increase targets.
Buckee said he doubted the target could be met because of a lack of avialable drilling rigs in western Canada.

"It's kind of nonsense," Proto said. "I guess I can be a little sarcastic in that one of the things he should know about Saskatchewan is that Saskatchewan's not exactly winter drilling country and we do most of our drilling in the last three quarters of the year."
He said that of the 284 operated wells Wascana drilled in 1996, 120 were drilled in the fourth quarter.
Eighty-five percent of the company's 460 budgeted wells in 1997 have summer access and its winter drilling program in northeast British Columbia and northwest Alberta was on track, Proto said.
Also, Wascana planned to drill its locations using 21 rigs throughout the year and had already contracted 18, he said.
Wascana has projected 1997 production to average 65,000 barrels per day of oil and 235 million cubic feet of natural gas, both large increases over 1996.

Proto said he was pleased that Buckee had pointed out in a conference call that Wascana's cash flow in 1996 would have increased by about 55 percent if it had not been for foregone revenues due to crude oil price hedging.
"I found that good, in that he recognized the real value in Wascana's assets," he said.
Wascana's board is required to make a recommendation to shareholders by March 13.
Wascana shares on Friday closed up 0.05 to 18.75. Talisman gained 0.30 to close at 44.45.
